diagnostic_evidence.quote: so that all terms in \eqref{eq:DF-ql} are controlled by H\"older's inequality together with the Sobolev

issues.failure_explanation: The terms ∫ ∂_s A δu·∇v and ∫ ∂_p B·∇δu v involve one factor in L^p (δu or v) and one in L^2 (∇v or ∇δu); Hölder requires the coefficient in L^r with 1/r = 1 − 1/p − 1/2, i.e. r = 2p/(p−2), not p/2. The two exponents agree only for p = 6. For any other admissible p (e.g. p = 4, used later) the stated 'sufficient set of assumptions' does not make the terms of (2.8) well defined, contrary to the prose claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exponent p/2 by 2p/(p−2) for ∂_s A and ∂_p B (or fix p = 6).
issues.overall_effect: The stated well-posedness conditions for D𝓕 in the quasilinear class are insufficient as written; no formal result depends on them, but the claimed sufficiency is false for p ≠ 6.
issues.title: Quasilinear integrability exponents for ∂_s A and ∂_p B do not close the Hölder estimate
issues.why_classification: A local exponent correction restores the claim with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: The standing assumption is f ∈ V* = H^{-1}(Ω). The residual representation (4.1) rewrites −⟨f,v⟩ as an elementwise integral of (c − f − ∇·σ_h) v, and Theorem 4.x bounds ‖𝓡_T(σ_h)‖_{L²(T)}. Neither is defined unless f (and c(·,ũ_h), resp. B(·,ũ_h,∇ũ_h)) belongs to L²(Ω). The theorem is stated without this hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis f ∈ L²(Ω) and c(·,ũ_h) ∈ L²(Ω) (resp. B(·,ũ_h,∇ũ_h) ∈ L²(Ω)) to Section 4 / Theorem thm:res-majorant.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:res-majorant (hence the (C1) certificate) is ill-defined for general f ∈ V*; it is valid only under an unstated L² regularity of the source and reaction terms (satisfied in the numerical example).
issues.title: Residual majorant uses L²(T) norms of element residuals containing f, but f is only assumed in V*
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard regularity hypothesis fixes the statement; the method, bound and numerics are unaffected.

Therefore, the $u$-dependent diffusion model \eqref{eq:quasi-u-diffusion} satisfies (C3) on $B_{\rho}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For d ∈ {2,3}, H_0^1(Ω) does not embed into L^∞(Ω), so no constant C_∞ with ‖v‖_∞ ≤ C_∞‖v‖_V exists, and B_ρ ⊂ H_0^1 contains unbounded functions, so M_∞(ρ) does not exist either. Every bound in Section 7.4 (eq:quasi-u-coeffdiff, eq:quasi-u-term1, eq:quasi-u-term2, eq:quasi-u-Lrho) uses these nonexistent constants, so the claimed Lipschitz estimate eq:quasi-u-C3 is vacuous. Moreover, the term ∫ ∂_s a(w) δu ∇w·∇v in eq:quasi-u-DF is not integrable for general δu,w,v ∈ H_0^1, so D𝓕(w) is not even a bounded operator V→V* for this model: the u-dependent diffusion problem does not fit the V = H_0^1 framework at all.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace V = H_0^1 by a space (or additional a priori regularity on B_ρ, e.g. W^{1,∞} control) in which a(·,w)∇w is differentiable and L^∞ control of the ball is available, and redo the Lipschitz estimate in that setting.
issues.overall_effect: The only quasilinear (C3) route in the paper is invalid; the claim that the u-dependent diffusion model satisfies (C3) on B_ρ, and thus that the NK certification applies to this quasilinear prototype, is unsupported. The semilinear results and numerics are unaffected.
issues.title: (C3) for u-dependent diffusion rests on a false L^∞ embedding of H_0^1
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the claim survives in the paper's functional setting; certifying u-dependent diffusion requires new architecture (different spaces/norms and embeddings), so the advertised quasilinear (C3) regime is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\sigma_h^{\ast}\in H(\div;\Omega)$ be any flux satisfying the (adjoint) divergence target $\div\sigma_h^{\ast}=r_h^{\ast}$ elementwise.

issues.failure_explanation: Inserting σ*_h into ⟨𝓖(z_h),v⟩ = ∫ψv − ∫A∇z_h·∇v − ∫∂_s c z_h v gives ∫(σ*_h − A∇z_h)·∇v + Σ_T ∫_T (ψ − ∂_s c z_h + ∇·σ*_h) v, i.e. the true element residual is s*_h + ∇·σ*_h, not s*_h − ∇·σ*_h. With the prescribed target ∇·σ*_h = Π_T^0 s*_h the true residual s*_h + Π_T^0 s*_h has element mean 2∫_T s*_h ≠ 0, so the mean-equilibration hypothesis of Theorem thm:res-majorant is violated and the displayed bound for ‖𝓖(z_h)‖_{V*} is not guaranteed. Consistency with the primal convention (eq:gh-def, where s_h = c − f corresponds to ∇·(A∇u) = c − f) requires s*_h := ∂_s c(·,ũ_h) z_h − ψ (equivalently ∇·σ*_h = −Π_T^0 s*_h).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine s*_h := ∂_s c(·,ũ_h) z_h − ψ (or set the divergence target to −Π_T^0 s*_h and the residual to s*_h + ∇·σ*_h), then Theorem thm:res-majorant applies verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The recipe for a guaranteed computable bound of ‖𝓖(z_h)‖_{V*} is incorrect as written; the adjoint-enhanced enclosures (Theorem thm:qoi:adjoint applied in Section 9, Tables tab:sec9-qoi-linear/quadratic) are only certified if the implementation used the correct sign, which the source does not confirm.
issues.title: Adjoint-residual flux construction uses the wrong sign in the divergence target, breaking mean equilibration
issues.why_classification: A one-line sign correction restores the construction and the guarantee with no loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: admissibility holds exactly for radius below $\rho_+$ and fails for radius at or above $\rho_+$

issues.failure_explanation: The intersection of the closed interval [ρ_-,ρ_+] (sublevel set of p) with (0,ρ_q) equals [ρ_-,ρ_+] (closed) whenever ρ_+ < ρ_q, not [ρ_-,min{ρ_+,ρ_q}). Using the theorem's p, at the upper root q(ρ_+) = 2 − 2η/ρ_+, which is < 1 exactly when ρ_+ < 2η, so this closed case does occur. Then Adm(sup 𝓐𝓓) is true, contradicting the lemma's assertions that 𝓐𝓓 = [ρ_-,ρ_+), that admissibility 'fails for radius at or above ρ_+', and that Adm fails on [ρ_*,ρ_up]. Also the degenerate case η = 0 gives ρ_- = 0, contradicting 0 < ρ_-. Separately, the appendix defines p with α^{-2} whereas Theorem thm:NK uses (2α)^{-1}, so the lemma nominally concerns a different function (the convexity argument is unaffected).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that 𝓐𝓓 is a (possibly closed) interval [ρ_-,ρ_+] or [ρ_-,ρ_+), assume η > 0 (or allow ρ_- = 0), replace strict by non-strict inequalities in the threshold description and in Case 1 of prop:alg-rho-correct, and align the appendix's p with eq:pq.
issues.overall_effect: The precise interval-structure statement of lem:adm-interval is false in a boundary regime; Proposition prop:alg-rho-correct's conclusions (bracket invariant with ≤, admissible return value) remain valid with non-strict inequalities, so Algorithm alg:rho still returns an admissible radius.
issues.title: Admissible set is not always half-open; lemma's threshold description fails when the p-constraint binds
issues.why_classification: Local restatement with non-strict inequalities preserves the algorithm's correctness and all guarantees.
